author: Times News
description:
“It’s that kind of incident that is seared in the national consciousness.”

On 16 October 2020, French school teacher Samuel Paty was murdered by a Russian Muslim refugee after a false accusation of blasphemy started a vicious harassment campaign. Six years on, the incident has left Paty’s family feeling “abandoned” by authorities that failed to recognise the risks to his life, says The Sunday Times’s Europe editor, Peter Conradi.

Peter Conradi was speaking to Jane Mulkerrins on Times Radio. Listen live every Saturday, from 1-4pm.
